about: P3 quota source manifest (bound annex), established under owner decision 5 (docs/design/ozmap-replication-2026-10-24/owner-decisions.md, item 5): the D5 causal coverage of earlier groups is replaced by a static headroom bound. Implemented in bench/ozmap_rep/quota.py (read_file, owner_problem, headroom_m, headroom_gate, estimate_m) and run.CellRun.codex_quota_gate; tests in bench/ozmap_rep/tests/test_p3_headroom.py. The unbound candidate P3-quota-source-manifest-candidate.json (D5, not_established) stays as the record of the D5 work.

account_field_mapping.baseline: isolation.account_sha256(baseline): sha256 of tokens.account_id of the baseline auth.json, else the chatgpt_account_id claim of its id_token or access_token
account_field_mapping.enforced_by: quota.attribution_problem, called by quota.coverage_gate for the owner reading and every harvested reading
account_field_mapping.evidence: the newest 30 owner rollouts, by CLI version and account attribution (hash comparison only, 2026-10-25): 0.163.0-alpha.11.2 account=none: 6 files, 0 readings; 0.160.0 account=baseline: 23 files, 69 readings; 0.164.0-alpha.11.1 account=baseline: 1 files, 180 readings. No rollout carries another account.
account_field_mapping.finding: the owner sessions directory also receives rollouts of other CLI builds (0.163.0-alpha and 0.164.0-alpha, the desktop app). The 0.163.0-alpha rollouts carry no creator_account_id. Before the repair of 2026-10-25 quota.coverage_gate accepted such a reading, because it rejected an account mismatch only when both hashes were present (Astra A blocker P3, Opus B blocker OB-P3).
account_field_mapping.readings_from_other_cli_versions: a reading from a CLI build other than the pinned one is accepted only with the same account hash, limit_id and window; its timestamp semantics are those of the pinned build only by assumption
account_field_mapping.rollout: the session_meta event (type session_meta) payload.creator_account_id, hashed with sha256
account_field_mapping.rule: a reading counts only when both the baseline account hash and the reading account hash are present and equal; a reading without an account hash is not attributable and blocks, and an unknown baseline account hash blocks every reading (quota.attribution_problem, owner and harvested readings alike)

bucket_identity.enforced_by: quota.read_file records limit_id and window_minutes; quota.attribution_problem rejects other values
bucket_identity.evidence: 249 readings in the newest 30 owner rollouts: limit_id always codex, primary.window_minutes always 10080, secondary always null
bucket_identity.rule: a reading counts only when rate_limits.limit_id is exactly codex and primary.window_minutes is the integer 10080 (config.QUOTA_LIMIT_ID, config.QUOTA_WINDOW_MINUTES); any other or missing value blocks

coverage_predicate_implemented.d5_text: before a synchronized Codex dispatch group, every previously completed live Codex attempt that could have consumed the baseline quota (quota.needs_coverage) is covered by a validated, attributable reading whose rollout session started strictly after the attempt ended (ended_at, else ended_at_upper; an attempt with neither is never covered). The floor is the event timestamp of the session_meta event of that rollout, and a task_started event must precede the reading in its own turn; a session or turn start in the future or after the reading blocks the gate. Candidate readings are the latest owner reading and the harvested worker readings of other attempts. A reading never covers the attempt whose own rollout produced it, and a concurrent sibling is never covered by another worker of its group, because both sessions started before either ended. The gate percent is the maximum of the latest owner reading, every covering reading and every valid harvested reading; at least 80 stops.
coverage_predicate_implemented.status: superseded by owner decision 5 (headroom_bound); quota.coverage_gate stays in the code and its uncovered list is recorded per gate as d5_uncovered_informational, without blocking

evidence.item: codex.exe 0.160.0 holds the header names x-codex-primary-used-percent, -primary-window-minutes and -primary-reset-at and the TokenCountEvent rate_limits field; no persisted rate limit cache string (latest_rate_limits) was found

An attempt ending at 03:23:00 lies inside this turn; the bound event time rule covered it, D5 does not (test_real_an_attempt_ending_inside_an_owner_turn_is_not_covered_by_it)

bench/ozmap_rep/tests/test_p3_d5_coverage.py: the Opus B repro of signoff-opus-2.md now blocks; own rollout, concurrent siblings, sequential groups, long sessions, missing or inconsistent starts, unsettled and recovered attempts, maximum percent, freshness

freshness_and_causal_coverage.basis: owner decision 5 (owner-decisions.md item 5, commit cd83fe4): causal coverage of the latest call group cannot be established without a model call or an authenticated rate limit request, so the driver, under the owner's delegation, replaced it with the static headroom bound below. P3 is established when this manifest records the bound, m with its sources, and U0 at launch.
freshness_and_causal_coverage.freshness: the freshness_rule below (owner reading at most 60 minutes old), unchanged
superseded_open_points: server side accounting lag: whether a request that started after an attempt ended already sees that attempt in x-codex-primary-used-percent. The fixtures show monotone readings and a rise within minutes, but at one point resolution they cannot bound the lag, and measuring it needs a model call, which P3 forbids

signatory acceptance: Astra A did not approve D5 or the 60 minute rule (signoff-astra-2.md); Opus B approved the freshness rule only with point 2, which this candidate implements; both must sign a manifest whose status is established

operational consequence (Opus B D5 point 4): workers keep --ephemeral, so the only covering source on the live route is an owner session that starts after the previous group ended. A worker rollout can never cover the group immediately before the gate, because its session starts before that group ends. Without an independently authorized owner Codex call between groups, the run stops after the telemetry group (a stop under A4.14.1)

freshness_rule.basis: implementer proposal of 2026-10-25, accepted by Opus B as a selection bound with D5 point 2 (rulings/signoff-opus-2.md); not approved by Astra A (rulings/signoff-astra-2.md). It is config.QUOTA_OWNER_MAX_AGE_MINUTES
freshness_rule.text: the latest owner reading (the last rate_limits object of the newest owner session file) is always required, must carry an event timestamp and blocks when that timestamp is more than 5 minutes after the gate time (future) or more than 60 minutes before it (stale). Harvested worker readings never replace it. Covering readings of older attempts need no freshness of their own: the gate also takes the fresh owner reading and the maximum of every reading. File modification times are never freshness evidence.

headroom_bound.C: the remaining Codex call allowance under A4.5, evaluation plus telemetry: EVAL_CAPS codex total (62) minus every physical Codex call charged so far in the experiment (run.CellRun.codex_remaining_calls, the experiment ledger plus the run directory)
headroom_bound.U0: the latest owner reading (quota.owner_problem: present, valid, event timestamped, not in the future, baseline account hash, limit_id codex, primary window 10080, at most 60 minutes before the gate), raised to the maximum of every valid harvested worker reading (none while workers keep --ephemeral)

U0_at_establishment.note: the window reset at 15:02:28 UTC; this is not the launch reading, which the run records itself

headroom_bound.U0_at_launch: recorded by every gate row in evidence/quota-gates.jsonl of the live run directory (fields u0, u0_owner, owner_reading_at, owner_source, m, remaining_calls, factor, bound); the launch value is the row with group pre-cell of the telemetry cell
headroom_bound.enforced_by: run.CellRun.gates (group pre-cell, before every live Codex cell, the telemetry cell included, which is the launch) and run.CellRun.reserve_group (before every dispatch group, under the authentication lock); both call quota.headroom_gate with m from quota.headroom_m, which reads this manifest through config.SIGNED_RULINGS. A missing or invalid m blocks.
headroom_bound.m_unit: percentage points of primary used_percent per physical Codex call of the route

assumptions: used_percent is monotone within one reset window (no decrease in any preserved reading)

a reading reflects at most the consumption accounted when its request started; the upper reading was taken 28 minutes after the latest possible end of the last pilot call, so an accounting lag below 28 minutes is covered

three pilot calls (two telemetry calls of live-6a518ece47ab and call a5a07e4405 of codex-boolq-A, all process_error) carry no usage; they are counted in N and left out of the token shares, which raises every share; their elapsed times (11.8 s, 12.1 s, 66.6 s) are below that of the longest call with usage (83.9 s)
quota consumption of a call is at most proportional to one of the three token weightings; the factor 2 of the bound is the margin for calls heavier than the largest pilot call
method.text: quota.estimate_m. The pilot ran every Codex call with --ephemeral, so no rollout of the route holds a reading of its own. Its consumption is bracketed by owner readings of the same account and bucket: the latest reading before the first pilot call was reserved and the earliest reading from a session that started after the last call could have ended (reservation plus the 1320 s child timeout). The rise between them plus the one point reading resolution is an upper bound on what all calls inside consumed together; other consumption in the interval (the tail of an owner Astra call, the owner desktop app) only raises it. m is that bound times the largest share of one call: 1/N, and the share of the largest call in the tokens of the calls with usage under three weightings (input plus output, uncached input plus output, output only); the maximum, rounded up to 0.01.

headroom_bound.pre_cell_owner_reading_check: the D5 owner reading check (quota.owner_problem) stays as an additional gate in both places: no owner reading, an invalid, unattributable, future or stale one stops before the bound is evaluated
headroom_bound.rule: a live Codex cell and every synchronized Codex dispatch group are released only when U0 + factor x C x m < stop_percent and U0 < stop_percent

repairs.2026-10-25: blockers P3 and OB-P3 (see the bound manifest)
repairs.2026-10-25 D5: strict causal coverage predicate with the session floor (this candidate)
repairs.2026-10-25 owner decision 5: static headroom bound in place of the D5 causal coverage; status established (this manifest)

selection_and_validation: select the latest relevant reading first, then validate it; a malformed latest reading blocks and an older valid reading is never substituted
reject missing evidence, booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite values, values outside [0, 100], unexplained future timestamps, account or bucket mismatches
no model call is added, repeated or relabeled to obtain a reading; no stale reading exception; the only headroom rule is headroom_bound (owner decision 5)

reject a reading without an account hash, or when the baseline account hash is unknown; reject limit_id other than codex and window_minutes other than 10080; reject a reading without an event timestamp; reject a stale owner reading (freshness_rule)

sources.owner_rollout: ~/.codex/sessions/*/*/*/*.jsonl of the owner (same account): the newest file by modification time is selected (selection only, never freshness evidence) and its LAST rate_limits object is the reading
sources.worker_rollout: CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl of the worker home of one attempt; exists only when the worker argv omits --ephemeral (P3); harvested by Isolation.finish before the home is emptied; only percent, event timestamp, account hash and CLI version leave the credential boundary

timestamp_semantics.field: the top level timestamp of the rollout event that carries rate_limits (ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix)
timestamp_semantics.future: a timestamp more than 5 minutes after the gate time blocks
timestamp_semantics.meaning: when the CLI recorded the token_count event of a turn; it is emitted inside the call, before the call ends
timestamp_semantics.never: file modification times are never freshness evidence (P3)
timestamp_semantics.request_start: codex-cli 0.160.0 parses the x-codex-primary-used-percent, x-codex-primary-window-minutes and x-codex-primary-reset-at response headers (strings of codex.exe); a reading therefore reflects at most the consumption the server had accounted when the request that returned it started
timestamp_semantics.session_floor: the top level timestamp of the session_meta event; in the 0.160.0 exec fixtures it precedes task_started by 0 to 4 ms

value_semantics.monotonicity: within one reset window (same primary.resets_at) no observed reading decreased across 249 readings
value_semantics.resolution: every observed value is a whole number (float type), so the reading has one percentage point resolution
value_semantics.valid: a finite JSON number in [0, 100] that is not a boolean (quota.valid_percent)
